page.layout: One column of running text, with small marginal marks in the right margin. The left margin holds only the edge of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed. Running head and page number at the top, signature at the foot.

main_text.p: his erant qui judicia varia exercebant, qui pecuniam publicam tractabant, qui civium mores curabant censebantque, qui societatibus civilibus, in quas civitas erat distincta, præerant, & id genus alii. Et quia civitas rebus maritimis propter portuum commoditatem, multum dedita erat, non pauci regundis iis quotannis præficiebantur. Verùm ætatem diu ferre status iste non potuit. Erat enim nimium popularis, in quo minimum ii, qui sapientiâ præstabant, plurimum improvidi & stulti valebant, ἀπερίσκεπτοι γὰρ ἢ ἀνοητότεροι οἱ πολ-λοί[?]: qui ut ferè per se minus periti sunt negociorum publicorum, ita minus quoque ad ea, quæ publicè aguntur, animos advertunt, singulí vero sua potissimum spectant & curant, iisque occupatas mentes habent. Quapropter facillimè ab illis, qui astutiâ pollent, in fraudem abducuntur. Quod hoc accidit evidentissimè. Nam vixdum ocnio exacto post Athenienses in Siciliâ debellatos, & reipublicæ potestatem Syracusis ad populum traductam, Dionysius Hermocratis filius, vir vaferrimi ingenii, simulator egregius, dementat plebe, & corporis sui custodiâ validâ ea impetratâ, tyrannidem invasit, cum flueret annus LXI post rempublicam

page.notes: Right margin: short marks beside the lines "ocnio" to "rempublicam" (in roughly the order: ΙΑ, ΕΙΙ(), ΥΥ, ΥΑ, ΑΙΙ, ΕΙΙ(), ΥΥ, ΥΑ, ΥΥ) are too damaged to read; they are probably marginal marks or abbreviations and are not transcribed. Some are visible at the bottom right, unreadable. The catchword at the bottom right is unreadable and not transcribed. The first Greek word is uncertain (ἀπερίσκεπτοι assumed from context), so it is marked [?]. The word "ocnio" in the last-but-one line is a misprint or damage for "exacto"; the printed text was read as "exacto". Left margin: edge of the neighbouring page, not transcribed.
